interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 1, uma para cada quantidade (rotuladas "Shandell's growth" e "Nicole's growth"); para cada reta há um campo onde o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividi-la (com confirmação) e, depois, marca o ponto da fração correspondente; abaixo, um seletor em que o aluno escolhe UMA destas alternativas: "Shandell grew more."; "Nicole grew more."; "Both grew the same amouth."; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir cada reta, marcar cada ponto, escolher a alternativa, concluir).

segunda reta numérica; o aluno marca o ponto da segunda fração
seletor com as alternativas de comparação; o aluno escolhe uma delas

dicas.texto: Which number in a fraction tells how many equal parts make up the whole?
Look at the bottom number in Shandell's fraction and use it to set the number of equal divisions.
The denominator in Shandell's fraction is the number you should enter in the denominator field.
Enter the bottom number of 5/... in the field and confirm the division of the line.
What does the numerator tell you to count on the divided number line?
Start at zero and count equal intervals using the denominator as the size of the whole.
Move five equal intervals from zero on Shandell's number line.
Place the marker at the point reached after counting five of the twelve equal intervals.
Which part of a fraction tells how many equal sections the whole has?
Read Nicole's fraction and use its denominator to set the number of equal divisions.
Nicole's fraction has 2 as its bottom number.
Enter Nicole's denominator in the denom2 field and confirm the two-part division.
What does the numerator tell you to count from zero?
Use the two equal sections to identify the location of one selected part.
Count one equal interval from zero on Nicole's number line.
Place the marker at the first division after zero, which represents one of the two equal parts.
On a number line, which fraction represents the greater amount: the point farther left or the point farther right?
Compare the locations of both marked points on the two equal-length number lines.
Look carefully at which marked point is closer to 1.
Choose the person whose marked point is farther to the right on the number line.
Review what each marked point represents before completing the activity.
Use the comparison result from the two number lines, then choose the requested statement in compBox.
Check that your selected statement matches the final fraction recorded for Shandell.
Select the specified comparison statement, click Done, and let the tutor record Shandell's fraction.

exercicio.statement:
Shandell and Nicole are not the same height, but they both grew quite a lot since they started sixth grade this year. They are comparing their amount of growth to see who has grown more. Use the number line to find out.
Shandell grew 5/12 of an inch.
Nicole grew 1/2 an inch.
Who has grown more?
